output.summary: Evergreen tree-like cycad of unspecified native origin, found around Madagascar, nearby western Indian Ocean islands and parts of coastal East Africa. Its young leaves have a distinctive bluish tint, and its seeds contain a spongy layer that lets them float. Although toxic, the seeds are eaten on Ngazidja after repeated washing, fermentation and drying remove their cyanotoxins.
output.edibilityNote: On Ngazidja, toxic seeds are made edible by repeated washing, fermentation and drying to remove cyanotoxins.
